title: Delegation of Authority Matrix Update Notification Failure
scenario_text:
In February 2026, NovaTerra's CFO approved a capital expenditure of $2.8M for HVAC replacement at the Riverpoint Tower property. The expenditure was processed through Yardi, approved in the standard workflow, and the vendor (Apex Mechanical Services) has completed 60% of the work. An internal audit has now flagged the approval as potentially unauthorized.

**Shared Network Drive — \\ntserver\governance\DOA-matrix-2025.xlsx (Last modified: September 15, 2025)**
Row 12: 'Capital expenditures — single property' | Threshold: '$0-$1M: Property Manager | $1M-$3M: CFO | $3M+: Board approval' | Effective: January 2025

**SharePoint — /governance/policies/delegation-of-authority (Page version 3, published January 5, 2026)**
Section 4.1: Capital Expenditure Approvals
'$0-$500K: Property Manager | $500K-$1.5M: SVP Asset Management | $1.5M-$3M: CEO + CFO joint approval | $3M+: Board'
[Version 2 (September 2025) stated: '$0-$1M: Property Manager | $1M-$3M: CFO | $3M+: Board']
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @victoria.ashworth, December 18, 2025]: 'Updated per board directive from Dec 12 meeting. Tightening CapEx authority. Need to communicate to all budget holders before Jan 1 effective date.'

**Diligent Board Portal — Board Meeting Minutes (December 12, 2025)**
Item 7: 'The Board discussed tightening delegated authority for capital expenditures in light of recent overruns. RESOLVED that the Delegation of Authority matrix be updated to require joint CEO/CFO approval for expenditures between $1.5M and $3M, effective January 1, 2026. The Corporate Secretary is directed to update the DOA matrix and communicate changes to all affected personnel.'

**Outlook — From: Victoria Ashworth to all-budget-holders@novaterra.com (DRAFT — never sent)**
Subject: 'IMPORTANT: Updated Delegation of Authority — Effective January 1, 2026'
Body: 'Dear colleagues, Please be advised that per Board Resolution dated December 12, 2025, the following changes to capital expenditure approval thresholds are effective immediately...'
Status: Draft (saved December 22, 2025, never sent)

**Microsoft Teams — #asset-management (January 22, 2026, 3:15 PM)**
@frank.novak (SVP Asset Management): Hey team — heads up, I think the CapEx thresholds changed. Saw something on SharePoint but not sure if it's final. Anyone get an official notice?
@sarah.winters: I didn't see anything. Still going by the matrix on the shared drive.
@frank.novak: Probably just a draft. I'll ask Victoria next time I see her.
[No further messages]

**Yardi Voyager — CapEx Approval Workflow / Riverpoint Tower HVAC (February 8, 2026)**
Project: HVAC Full Replacement | Budget: $2,800,000 | Submitted by: Property Manager, Riverpoint
Approval Chain (as configured in system): Property Manager > CFO
Approved by: CFO (Thomas Hartwell) on February 10, 2026
System note: 'Approval routing based on DOA matrix loaded September 2025.'

**Outlook — From: Thomas Hartwell (CFO) to Victoria Ashworth (June 20, 2026)**
Subject: 'RE: Audit Finding — Riverpoint HVAC CapEx'
'Victoria — I was never notified of any DOA change. The matrix on the shared drive still shows my single approval is sufficient up to $3M. I approved this in good faith based on the policy I had access to. When was this supposedly communicated?'
question: Based on the corporate governance records, what is the correct determination regarding the validity of the CFO's February 2026 approval of the $2.8M HVAC expenditure?

contributor.name: Victoria Ashworth
contributor.title: Corporate Secretary & Governance Director
contributor.domain_expertise: Board resolutions, delegation of authority, signatory verification, corporate entity management

choices: The approval is invalid — the board resolution is effective January 1, 2026 regardless of communication; board resolutions are binding on all officers from the date specified, and the CFO should have checked the board portal

The approval is valid — the updated DOA was never formally communicated to budget holders, the notification email was never sent, and the Yardi system still reflected the old thresholds; the CFO acted reasonably based on available information

The approval is invalid but curable — the CEO can provide retroactive co-approval to ratify the expenditure under the new DOA matrix, since the substantive threshold (CEO + CFO joint) can still be met

The approval is valid — the SharePoint page is marked as 'version 3' but the shared drive matrix (the system of record referenced in Yardi's workflow configuration) was never updated, meaning the old policy remained operative
